column1: # One throwaway git repo per row. `base` is committed, then the row takes a
# PRE-fix snapshot through the classifier's own `--snapshot` mode - so every row
# exercises that path - then `work` is written to the working tree, then the
# untracked file lands, then `ops` runs, then the classifier runs as
# `<repo-root> <pre-tree>`. The snapshot sits at the commit here, so a row's
# delta is what `git diff HEAD` used to show; the bespoke cases at the end of
# the runner are where the snapshot moves off HEAD.
# Columns: name  path  base  work  untracked  ops  expected_stdout  expected_stderr
#   path       one file, or several separated by `|`
#   base       file content at HEAD; \n is a newline. One value per `path`.
#   work       working-tree content; `=` leaves the file untouched, `@DEL@`
#   untracked  a path to create as an untracked file, or `-` for none
#   ops        one git operation applied after `work` is written, or `-`:
# Header shapes with no TSV-expressible input (new file mode, similarity index,
# Binary files, \ No newline at end of file, staged deltas, an ignored file, a
# linked worktree, a snapshot taken anywhere but the commit, an unresolvable
# pre-tree, a bare repo, a non-repo root) ride as bespoke cases at the end of
# --- content is counted per file, not across the delta (#476 defect 1) ------
# A 100%-similar rename emits no content lines at all, so a comment reword in
# ANOTHER file used to pay for it and the moved file went invisible.
# The snapshot seeds its throwaway index from the real one, so an index-only
# chmod is a mode change in the tree it writes, on every platform.
# --- a block comment that closes mid-line (#476 defect 4) -------------------
